subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should remote node-host `openclaw models auth login` fail closed before provider auth starts, or should OpenClaw implement authenticated gateway-side credential forwarding for this flow?
rationale: Both options change where sensitive provider credential material is acquired and stored across the node/gateway boundary, so automation should not choose that security boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail closed before auth starts
options.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with an actionable instruction to run the command on the gateway host while preserving accepted loopback/tunnel forms.

options.title: Forward credentials to gateway
options.body: Design and review a gateway RPC/setup flow that stores provider auth material on the gateway without first consuming tokens into the node-local store.

options.title: Warn but allow local writes
options.body: Warn node-host users that login affects only the node and accept the wrong-host credential risk for compatibility.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before auth starts
recommendation.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with an actionable instruction to run the command on the gateway host while preserving accepted loopback/tunnel forms.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent already authored and verified the maintainer repair direction for this exact remote-node auth guard.
